title: A list member is bounded by its maximum
statement: Let $s$ be a finite list of natural numbers and let $n$ belong to $s$. Then $n$ is at most the right fold of maximum over $s$ with initial value $0$.
replaced:
For a finite list $s$ of natural numbers, write $\max(s)$ for the right fold of
$\max$ over $s$ with initial value $0$ (so the empty list has maximum $0$). If $n$ is a
member of $s$, then $n \le \max(s)$.
